A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LATTE research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–H are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v3 reports original model fine-tuning results, benchmark comparisons, data ablations and error analyses in the main text and Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds inference ablations and newer-backbone comparisons in Tables 6–7.

M1.justification: The reasoning-trace structure, generation/filtering pipelines, training targets and action implementations are unchanged. GPT-backed OCR and the EasyOCR alternative already appear in v3's Listing 1; v4 tests existing components rather than introducing a revised method.

E1.justification: Training retains the Cauldron, Mantis-Instruct and Visual Genome sources. Evaluation retains the six main benchmarks and the additional appendix benchmarks, including A-OKVQA, MMMU and MMVP. New experiments vary models and inference settings without adding data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Vanilla IT, VPD, LLaVa-CoT, LLaVa-Plus and CogCoM, plus the unchanged appendix VisCoT comparison. The new backbone experiments reuse Vanilla IT as the comparator; the backbone names represent model configurations.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 adds configurations with 5/10/20 tool-call limits, disabled QUERYLANGUAGEMODEL and alternative OCR, plus InternVL3-8B and Qwen2.5VL-3B/7B backbones. These extend the existing evaluation framework; previously reported metrics, training settings and appendix evaluation defaults are retained.

E4.justification: New Section 4.3 substantially expands the diagnostic analyses by isolating dependence on language-model queries and OCR quality, testing inference-budget saturation and checking newer backbones. These controls were absent from v3; its data, hyperparameter and error analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and benchmark averages without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new experiments introduce no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 6–7 add substantive findings on tool dependence, call budgets and three newer backbones. Table 6 reports overall scores of 47.8 for default LATTE and no QUERYLM, 45.7 with EasyOCR, and 47.2/47.6 with 5/20 calls. These are newly reported conditions; matched earlier results remain unchanged. Table 7's aggregate inconsistencies limit interpretation of its added scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–2 defining LATTE-traces and the mathematical filtering criteria are unchanged. No new assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims about specialist-assisted reasoning, the reasoning-trace dataset, benchmark gains and data quality are retained. The abstract adds '4–5%' to its gains statement, but v3 already states that range in the introduction and Table 1.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly interprets QUERYLANGUAGEMODEL as unimportant for the evaluated benchmarks, attributes the EasyOCR degradation to less accurate outputs and suggests ten calls usually suffice. It also discusses applicability to stronger backbones. Existing mechanism explanations and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The new ablations document concrete configurations, including 5/20-call caps and disabling QUERYLANGUAGEMODEL. Existing implementation listings, prompts, training hyperparameters, hardware, licenses and artifact links remain unchanged. Both OCR implementations and the ten-turn default were already documented in v3.

R1.justification: The bibliography, related-work discussion and Appendix A comparison retain the same works and research positioning. The newer backbone experiments do not introduce new citations or revise the novelty argument.

P1.justification: v4 inserts an Additional ablations subsection, renumbers Error Analysis and adds an acknowledgment. The abstract and a few explanatory sentences receive limited edits; the broader narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds two compact tables and reflows existing material, including Table 4 and Figure 7. Subsequent tables are renumbered and some headers and caption formatting change. Existing figure graphics and the overall document design are retained.

improvement.justification: Table 6 adds useful inference controls, but the new backbone comparison introduces unresolved aggregation inconsistencies. In Table 7, InternVL3-8B LATTE has component scores of 54.1 and 54.5 but an Overall score of 52.0, inconsistent with the established averaging scheme. No per-benchmark results or explanation resolve this discrepancy. The useful added analysis and impaired reporting reliability leave the net quality change uncertain.
